clue.text: At first, 2 set out in this direction

definitions.note: the clue's own phrase points at the answer as a compass direction

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so these letters are rearranged
at first asks for only the opening letter of the name that 2 stands for

parts.note: 2-down is ALICE, whose first letter is wanted
taken as written

explanation.surface: Alice begins her adventure by setting off in a particular direction.
explanation.walkthrough: The 2 is a cross-reference to 2-down, the heroine of the puzzle's Alice in Wonderland theme.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four compass points, a heading in which a traveller may set off.

clue.text: After a piece of cake, no longer small — 15 and 17, she said

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: no longer small tells you the piece of cake loses the abbreviation for small, echoing the heroine growing after eating

parts.note: a slice is a portion cut from a cake
S is the standard abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: After eating a piece of cake, Alice grows and exclaims 'curiouser and curiouser'.
explanation.walkthrough: In Wonderland Alice eats a cake marked EAT ME and grows huge, then says 'Curiouser and curiouser!', the answers to 15 and 17.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Lewis Carroll's story famously utters the phrase 'Curiouser and curiouser' after growing enormously tall.

clue.text: Tweedledum (or Tweedledee?): "Save up for a washing machine"

parts.note: Tweedledum and Tweedledee are identical brothers in Through the Looking-Glass

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: save and but both mean except

explanation.surface: One of Carroll's comic brothers advises putting money by to buy a washer.
explanation.walkthrough: Save here is the preposition meaning except, not the verb about money. A twin-tub is an older British washing machine with separate washing and spinning drums.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin tub is a domestic laundry appliance with two separate drums, one for washing and one for spin-drying.

clue.text: Crazy about Disney's animation showing lots of faces

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word is wrapped around the other

parts.note: mad means crazy

indicators.note: animation brings letters to life and sets them moving into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; the possessive is just surface

explanation.surface: A fan wild about Disney cartoons, which show many characters' faces.
explanation.definitionFit: A many-sided solid has numerous flat surfaces, and the word also describes something with many aspects.

clue.text: Most seen baked dessert

indicators.note: baking transforms raw ingredients, so these letters are cooked up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The most commonly spotted baked pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton mess is not baked at all: it is crushed meringue, strawberries and cream, a British summer pudding named after Eton College.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton mess is a traditional English pudding of broken meringue, cream and strawberries served after the main course.

clue.text: Say no to girl that's 13, not 10

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name
13-across is IOWAN; without the IO that looks like 10 it leaves WAN, and wan means sallow

explanation.surface: Refusing a girl whose age is thirteen rather than ten.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers are cross-references, not ages: the IO at the start of 13's answer resembles the digits 10.
explanation.definitionFit: To disallow is to refuse permission or reject, as a referee rejects a goal, which is saying no.

clue.text: One's nothing to drink that might be radioactive

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for a thing which might be radioactive

parts.note: one is I, and 's is is
O is zero
tope is an old verb meaning to drink heavily

explanation.surface: A warning that a glass of something on offer may be dangerously radioactive.
explanation.definitionFit: An isotope is a form of an element with a different neutron count, and some such forms are unstable and emit radiation.

clue.text: 2 Diamonds discarded — outcome of rest changes

indicators.note: discarded means thrown away, so those letters are dropped from the name

parts.note: 2-down is the heroine's name
ice is slang for diamonds

indicators.note: an outcome is what something turns into, so the next word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bridge player discards two diamonds and the result of the remaining play shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-game surface makes 2 Diamonds look like a bridge bid; 2 is a cross-reference to 2-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Alters and changes are synonymous verbs in the third person, both meaning makes different or modifies.

clue.text: Knave of Hearts in tarts story, fit to be beheaded

indicators.note: beheading cuts off the head, so the opening letter of the word is removed
hearts are centres, so only the middle letter of each of the following words is used

parts.note: the central letter of tarts
the central letter of story
an ague is a fit of fever or shivering

explanation.surface: The Knave of Hearts, who stole the tarts in the Wonderland trial, deserves to lose his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knave of Hearts' reads as one character, but Hearts is the selection signal and Knave alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Knave is an old word for a dishonest scoundrel, and a rogue is likewise an unprincipled rascal.

clue.text: Starting point of book, by opening to rabbit hole

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so just that letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of rabbit
the letter O is shaped like a hole
OT, the Old Testament, is a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Alice's story begins when she falls down the rabbit hole.
explanation.walkthrough: By means next to: the book's letters sit beside the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A root is the origin or source from which something grows, the place where it begins.

clue.text: Firm desire to go back after that rabbit

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: a yen is a longing

explanation.surface: A company wants to return to chasing that rabbit.
explanation.definitionFit: Coney is an archaic English name for the rabbit, also used for its fur.

clue.text: Near darkness — no time to be seen

indicators.note: no, followed by to be seen, says the next item is absent from the longer word

parts.note: night is the dark time
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: As darkness approaches, there is no time left for being seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigh is an old-fashioned word for close by, as in 'the end is nigh'.

clue.text: 10 to 1 broadcast for statesman

parts.note: the digits 1 and 0 look like the letters I and O

indicators.note: broadcast means heard over the air, so the number is taken as it is spoken

parts.note: the number one, as spoken, is taken to sound like wan

explanation.surface: A broadcast hours before eleven, timed for some politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Statesman is read as state's man: a man from a US state, here Iowa. The sound match needs an accent where one rhymes with wan.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iowan is a native of the American state of Iowa, so cryptically a man of that state.

clue.text: Sound of car wheel?

parts.note: Audi is a German car make
the letter O is round like a wheel

explanation.surface: A question about the noise a car's wheel makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio refers to recorded or transmitted sound, as opposed to video or pictures.

clue.text: More interested in bric-a-brac addict?

definitions.note: the clue's question mark admits the comparative sense differs: more inquisitive

parts.note: a curio is an ornamental knick-knack
a user is a drug addict

explanation.surface: Someone hooked on junk-shop ornaments is more fascinated than most.
explanation.walkthrough: Read in as part of the charade: the answer is a curio user, someone addicted to bric-a-brac.
explanation.definitionFit: Curious means inquisitive or eager to know, so its comparative form describes greater inquisitiveness.

clue.text: Bit of a bloomer from stupid topless model, missing second day

indicators.note: topless means with the top removed, so the opening letter goes
missing means lacking, so the following items are taken away

parts.note: dumb is informal for stupid
taken as written
a mo is a moment, a second
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A tabloid tale of a gaffe by a dim-witted topless model who skipped a day.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer looks like a blunder, but here it is something that blooms, a flower; an umbel is part of one.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbel is a flat-topped flower cluster on stalks from one point, part of a flowering plant like cow parsley.

clue.text: Stranger wrecked our cruise

indicators.note: something wrecked is broken apart, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An unknown person sank our holiday voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: Stranger looks like a noun for an unknown person; it is the comparative adjective. Alice says 'Curiouser and curiouser' with 15.
explanation.definitionFit: Curious can mean odd or peculiar, so its comparative describes something odder or more peculiar.

clue.text: Dancing nude with elf, it's essential

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and settle in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone insists that dancing naked alongside a fairy is a must.
explanation.definitionFit: Needful is a formal word for required or necessary, what cannot be done without.

clue.text: Doctor entertained by 2 playing harpsichords

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is held within the host's home
playing with letters means moving them about into a new arrangement

parts.note: 2-down is the heroine's name
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor is entertained by Alice performing on keyboard instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Cembalo is the Italian name for the harpsichord, and cembali is its Italian plural form.

clue.text: Haul girl up who's falling behind

definitions.note: a phrase standing for the person who is falling behind

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are written from bottom to top

parts.note: to drag is to haul
gal is informal for girl

explanation.surface: Pulling up a girl who is lagging behind the others.
explanation.definitionFit: A laggard is a slowcoach, someone who dawdles and trails the rest of the group.

clue.text: Lot more quavers in this musical effect

indicators.note: to quaver is to tremble or waver, so these letters shake into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Many more short notes appear in this piece of musical ornamentation.
explanation.walkthrough: Quavers looks like the musical note; it is the verb meaning trembles, which also fits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremolo is a wavering, trembling sound produced by rapid repetition of a note, a performance device in music.

clue.text: Volume condensed into trickle

parts.note: surface reading: a large amount of liquid reduced to a mere dribble
setter's reading: the metric unit shrunk to its abbreviation KL, which sits inside the word trickle

explanation.surface: A great volume of liquid reduced to a mere dribble.
explanation.walkthrough: Condensed means abbreviated: the symbol for a thousand litres is kl, and those two letters appear in the middle of trickle.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilolitre is a metric measure of capacity, one thousand litres or a cubic metre.

clue.text: Girder builder erected, starting in early morning according to Cheshire Cat's statement?

indicators.note: in places those letters inside the time phrase that follows

parts.note: 1am, written as I AM, is an early hour of the morning

indicators.note: starting picks out the opening letter of each of the two preceding words

parts.note: the first letter of builder
the first letter of erected

explanation.surface: A girder put up by a builder at dawn, as the grinning Cheshire Cat might say.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 in 1AM is read as the letter I. The Cheshire Cat is famous for grinning, so it might well say 'I beam'.
explanation.definitionFit: An I-beam is a steel girder whose cross-section is shaped like a capital I, and 'I beam' means I smile broadly.

clue.text: Straighten a queue, say

indicators.note: say means spoken out loud, so the phrase is matched by its sound

parts.note: a queue is a line of people

explanation.surface: An instruction to tidy up a queue of people.
explanation.definitionFit: To align is to bring things into a straight row or correct position, so to straighten them.

clue.text: Scatter a little rosemary in casserole

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the dish word that follows

parts.note: a casserole is a stew

indicators.note: a little of a word is just a small part, its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of rosemary

explanation.surface: A cooking tip: sprinkle a pinch of rosemary into the casserole.
explanation.definitionFit: To strew is to spread or sprinkle things loosely over a surface, as one strews petals.

clue.text: See 5
Drink shorts with ice? Gin, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of each word is used

parts.note: the initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A query about whether spirits come on the rocks, mainly gin.
explanation.walkthrough: Shorts are British slang for spirits served in small measures, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: A swig is a large gulp of liquid, and to swig is to gulp a beverage down.

clue.text: Not satisfied by Uncut's content? Replace it with another music mag

indicators.note: replace means swap out, so the inner part of the magazine name is exchanged for another title

parts.note: the inner letters of Uncut, a British music magazine
the NME, New Musical Express, is another British music paper

explanation.surface: A reader unhappy with a music magazine's articles demands a rival title instead.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncut and the NME are both British music magazines; the middle three letters of the first are swapped for the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmet describes a demand or need that has not been fulfilled, so it remains unsatisfied.

clue.text: Number one veg, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard or told, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a leek is an onion-family vegetable

explanation.surface: The top-ranked vegetable, so we hear.
explanation.walkthrough: Number one looks like top spot; it is the childish term for a wee, and a leak is British slang for urinating.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a leak is slang for urinating, which children call doing a number one.

clue.text: Where scientists prove fat's not fine

indicators.note: not says the following item is absent from the word before it

parts.note: flab is fat, and 's adds an S
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Researchers demonstrating that fat is bad for you.
explanation.definitionFit: Laboratories are the workplaces where researchers run experiments to test and demonstrate their hypotheses.

clue.text: Space probe started to anger group of countries under one ruler

definitions.text: group of countries under one ruler

parts.note: an em is a printer's space

indicators.note: started points to the beginning of the preceding word, its first letter only

parts.note: the first letter of probe
ire is anger, and can be a verb meaning to anger

explanation.surface: A space probe launched to provoke a hostile power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Space probe' reads as one spacecraft; an em is the width of a letter M, a printing term.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is a number of nations or territories ruled by a single monarch or state.

clue.text: "No larks", ordered Ed and Isabel

indicators.note: ordered means put into a fresh arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ed and Isabel are told to stop their mucking about.
explanation.walkthrough: Larks look like pranks, but a lark is an early riser; a lie-abed sleeps late, the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-abed is a person who stays in bed late, the opposite of an early riser or lark.
